transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because the district added this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on top of my regular teaching load. I’m still getting through the day, but I feel constantly wound up and discouraged, which isn’t really like me. And I’ve started putting off lesson plans and emails that I normally would just handle without thinking twice.
Did these feelings start after the new bilingual social-emotional learning rollout was added to your workload?
Yes. Within the first month or two after they added it on top of my regular load, I started feeling unlike myself. Before that, I was managing my usual work and commitments pretty well.
If the workload from the new rollout were removed, do you think these feelings would mostly go away?
It’s hard to say for sure because the rollout is still ongoing. It hasn’t really ended, so I haven’t had the chance to see whether the feelings would go away afterward.
Outside of the new school rollout, have you been worrying a lot about other parts of your life too?
Not really. Most of my worry has been tied to the extra demands at school, not other areas of my life.
Have you been getting less pleasure from things you usually enjoy?
I’m not sure I’ve really noticed that. I still enjoy the things I usually do when I have the chance.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I’m not sure I’d say depressed most days. I’ve been stressed, but I haven’t really noticed feeling down all the time.
Do you find it hard to control the worrying?
I’m not really sure. I do worry about the school stuff, but I haven’t noticed whether it feels hard to control exactly.
Have these feelings been making it hard for you to do your job or manage things day to day?

I’m still teaching and keeping up with the basic responsibilities, but I’ve put off some planning deadlines. A couple of colleagues have had to remind me about things I used to get done reliably on my own.
Does your reaction to the new school rollout feel stronger than you would normally expect for that kind of work stress?

Yes, I think so. The bilingual social-emotional rollout got added on top of my regular teaching, and I’m still getting through the days, but I feel much more wound up and discouraged than I normally would. I’ve even been putting off lesson plans and emails that I used to just handle without thinking twice.
Have you been feeling hopeless?
I’m not sure I’d call it hopeless. I’ve been discouraged about it, but I don’t know that I’ve really felt hopeless.
Have you been feeling nervous or anxious most days?
Yes, most days since they added the rollout. I feel wound up about all of it, even though I’m still getting through my teaching.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you felt down or depressed more days than not?
I’m not really sure. I’ve felt discouraged and stressed, but I haven’t noticed feeling down most days.
Have you been feeling this wound-up and anxious for at least six months?
No, it’s been about five months—since the district assigned me the rollout role in the middle of the year.
Have you been feeling physically restless or unable to relax?
Yes. I have a hard time settling down after school, and I keep putting off lesson plans and emails that I normally would just take care of.
During the past two weeks, have you felt sad or down most of the day?
I’m not sure I’d say most of the day. I’ve been stressed and discouraged, but I haven’t really noticed being sad all day like that.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
A little, yes. I’m still teaching and handling the basics, but I’ve been missing or putting off planning deadlines, and colleagues have had to remind me about things I used to stay on top of.
Have you been crying more than usual?
I haven’t really noticed that, no.
During the past two weeks, have you lost motivation for things you usually need or want to do?
A little. I’m still teaching and taking care of the basics, but I’ve put off planning deadlines and needed colleagues to remind me about things I used to handle reliably.
Have you been feeling worthless?
No, I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling worthless.
Have you been more irritable than usual?
Yes, a bit. Since they added that bilingual social-emotional program to my regular teaching load, I’ve been more wound up, and little things at work get under my skin more than they normally would.
